title: What Is 710?
seoTitle: What Is 710? Why July 10 Is Concentrate Day | Uforia Dispensary
description: Turn 710 upside down and it spells OIL. Here is how July 10 became an informal holiday for cannabis concentrates, plus a quick primer on the main styles.
lede: Write 710 on a piece of paper, turn it upside down, and it reads OIL. That simple bit of wordplay has turned July 10 into a day for celebrating cannabis concentrates.

sections.heading: Where the number comes from
sections.html:
Concentrates are often called oils, and the upside-down spelling made 710 an easy inside joke among people who enjoy them. Its exact origin is hard to pin down, but the idea seems to have caught on in the early 2010s, as dabbing grew more popular. Dabbing simply means vaporizing a small amount of concentrate on a heated surface and inhaling the vapor.

Once the number had a meaning, the date followed naturally. July 10, written 7/10, became a day to celebrate extracts and the people who make them. If 420 is the holiday for cannabis culture as a whole, 710 is its younger sibling with a narrower focus.

sections.heading: What counts as a concentrate
sections.html:
A concentrate is any cannabis product that gathers the plant's cannabinoids and terpenes into a stronger form, leaving most plant material behind. There are many styles, and their names usually describe their texture or how they are made:

  • Live resin: extracted from fresh-frozen plants for a bright, aromatic profile.
  • Rosin: a solventless extract pressed out with heat and pressure.
  • Shatter and wax: named for their textures, from glassy and brittle to soft and crumbly.
  • Distillate: a highly refined oil often found in vape cartridges and edibles.
  • Hash and kief: traditional concentrates made from collected trichomes.

For a closer look at a few of these, read live resin vs rosin and what is kief?

sections.heading: How people mark the day
sections.html:
For many enthusiasts, 710 is a chance to try a style they have not tasted before, compare a live resin and a rosin from the same strain, or simply share a relaxed session with friends. Some people use a traditional dab rig, while others prefer an electronic dab device or a vape cartridge, neither of which needs a torch.

Like 420, it is an informal holiday rather than an official one. It has grown mostly through word of mouth, social media and a steady rise in curiosity about extracts.

sections.heading: Enjoying concentrates thoughtfully
sections.html:
Concentrates are much stronger than flower, so a tiny amount goes a long way. If they are new to you, start low and go slow, and give yourself time before deciding whether you want more. Many people find that lower temperatures bring out more flavor, while very high heat can taste harsh.

If you use a torch, keep it away from anything flammable and let hot glass and metal cool fully before touching them. Store concentrates in their original labeled containers, somewhere cool and out of reach of children and pets. Our safe consumption page has more tips, and when you are ready to explore, browse the concentrates and vaporizers on Uforia's live menu.

takeaways: 710 reads OIL upside down, which is why it stands for cannabis concentrates.
July 10, written 7/10, is an informal holiday for extracts and dabbing.
Popular styles include live resin, rosin, shatter, wax, distillate and hash.
Concentrates are strong, so start low and go slow.
